step.goal: Analyze documentation gaps and evaluate significance of changes
step.critical: ANALYZE ONLY - no updates in this step
The SIGNIFICANCE evaluation is the KEY decision point
step.action: Initialize analysis tracking: {{analysis}} = { inline_issues: [], external_issues: [], is_significant: false, significance_reasons: [], suggested_feature_doc: null, suggested_conditions: [] }
step.critical: CHECK INLINE DOCS: Examine each changed file for documentation gaps
step.action:
For each file in {{changed_files}} (excluding deleted): Analyze based on file type and check for:
**JavaScript/TypeScript (.js, .ts, .jsx, .tsx):** - Exported functions without JSDoc - Classes without class-level documentation - Complex logic blocks without explanatory comments - Public API methods without parameter/return documentation
**Python (.py):** - Functions without docstrings - Classes without docstrings - Complex algorithms without comments
**Other languages:** - Apply equivalent documentation standards
For each issue found, record: { file: "[path]", line: [number], type: "missing_jsdoc|missing_docstring|missing_comment", element: "[function/class/method name]", severity: "required|recommended" }
Store issues in {{analysis.inline_issues}}
step.critical: CHECK EXTERNAL DOCS: Determine if README or docs/ need updates
step.action:
Analyze if external documentation updates are needed:
**README.md updates needed if:** - New user-facing feature added - New CLI commands or options - New environment variables - Breaking changes to existing behavior - New installation/setup requirements
**docs/ updates needed if:** - New API endpoints - New configuration options - New architectural components - Significant workflow changes
For each issue found, record: { file: "[README.md or docs/specific.md]", section: "[section name]", issue: "[what needs to be added/updated]", severity: "required|recommended" }
Store issues in {{analysis.external_issues}}
step.critical: SIGNIFICANCE EVALUATION: Determine if changes warrant a feature doc
step.action:
Evaluate each significance criterion against the changes:
**SIGNIFICANT - Should create feature doc (check all that apply):**
- [ ] **New architectural pattern**: A way of doing things that will be repeated Examples: New service pattern, new component architecture, new data flow Check: Do changes introduce a pattern others should follow?
- [ ] **New feature area**: A cohesive set of functionality Examples: Authentication system, export functionality, notification system Check: Is this a distinct capability that didn't exist before?
- [ ] **Complex integration**: External service, API, or system integration Examples: Payment provider, email service, third-party API Check: Do changes integrate with external systems?
- [ ] **Non-obvious decisions**: Why something was done a certain way Examples: Performance trade-offs, security considerations, compatibility choices Check: Are there decisions future developers need to understand?
- [ ] **Reusable pattern**: Code pattern others should follow Examples: Error handling pattern, validation approach, caching strategy Check: Should other developers copy this approach?
- [ ] **Configuration system**: New config options or environment setup Examples: New env vars, new config file format, feature flags Check: Do changes add configurable behavior?
- [ ] **Breaking changes**: Changes that affect how others use the code Examples: API changes, removed features, changed interfaces Check: Will existing code need updates?
- [ ] **Security implementation**: Auth, permissions, encryption patterns Examples: JWT handling, RBAC implementation, data encryption Check: Are security-sensitive patterns being established?
- [ ] **Performance optimization**: Non-obvious performance patterns Examples: Caching strategy, query optimization, lazy loading Check: Are there performance patterns to document?
- [ ] **Testing patterns**: New testing approaches or fixtures Examples: Mock patterns, test utilities, integration test setup Check: Are testing patterns being established?
**NOT SIGNIFICANT - Standard docs only:** - Bug fixes (single issue resolution) - Minor refactoring (code cleanup without behavior change) - Typo fixes - Dependency updates (unless major version with breaking changes) - Style/formatting changes - Single-file changes with no broader implications

check.action: Generate feature doc proposal: {{analysis.suggested_feature_doc}} = { filename: "docs/features/[descriptive-kebab-case-name].md", title: "[Descriptive Feature Title]", overview: "[2-3 sentence summary of what was built and why]", type: "[pattern|feature|integration|decision|security|performance]" }

Generate suggested conditions for conditional docs guide: {{analysis.suggested_conditions}} = [ "When working with [feature area]", "When implementing [related functionality]", "When modifying [affected components]", "When troubleshooting [specific issues]" ] Generate 3-5 specific, actionable conditions based on the actual changes.
IMPORTANT: Conditions must be SPECIFIC to this feature, not generic patterns. - BAD: "When implementing caching strategies" (too generic) - GOOD: "When implementing caching for remote config endpoints" - BAD: "When adding admin endpoints" (too generic) - GOOD: "When adding admin endpoints for the remote config module" - BAD: "When creating public API endpoints" (too generic) - GOOD: "When creating public endpoints for app configuration"
Always include the feature name or domain in the condition.

check.if: no inline_issues AND no external_issues AND NOT is_significant
check.output: All documentation is up to date!
